 View Comments Metro Weather Politics Sports Business Puzzles Rhode Island Globe Magazine Opinion Health care Arts Lifestyle Education Cambridge & Somerville Money, Power, Inequality Spotlight Technology Climate Cars Real Estate Events FORECAST Storms dump up to 6 inches of rain across Mass. and R.I. Here are the latest totals.
 The wet New England weather came after the longest dry stretch of the year and warm November temperatures in the 70s.
 Print this Article 
 View Comments Heavy rain on Friday caused flooding in many areas, including at Garrett's Family Market in Falmouth, above, on Cape Cod. Police were advising people to stay off the roads into the night. Falmouth Police Department After the longest dry stretch of 2026, two weather systems deluged Southeastern Massachusetts, Cape Cod, and parts of Rhode Island with up to 6 inches of non-stop rain and isolated downpours, causing flash flooding in the evening in New Bedford, Acushnet, and other areas. 
 Numerous roads were closed in both areas due to “significant flooding,” according to officials. On Saturday, the front will slowly drag over the Gulf of Maine, keeping the chance of scattered showers during the morning and lingering into the afternoon as they become more isolated. 
 Some of the top rainfall totals as of early Saturday include: 
 W. Wareham — 6.11 inches 
 New Bedford — 4.45 inches 
 Ashaway, R.I. — 4.42 inches 
 Woods Hole — 4.34 inches 
 East Falmouth — 3.74 inches 
 Acushnet — 3.72 inches 
 Norton — 3.64 inches 
 West Bridgewater — 3.61 inches 
 Attleboro — 3.55 inches 
 Charlestown, R.I. — 3.44 inches 
 Sharon — 3.33 inches 
 Hyannis — 2.95 inches 
 Chatham — 2.8 inches 
 Cranston, R.I. — 2.76 inches 
 Norwood — 2.68 inches 
 Boston — 2.64 inches 
 Saturday should see a few spotty showers lingering over Southern New England; otherwise, expect mostly cloudy skies. Boston Globe The 7-day forecast for the Boston area. Boston Globe EARLIER FORECAST: An advancing front stalled over coastal New England, with Greater Boston and much of the region seeing scattered showers since the morning. Most of the steady and heavy rain has stayed concentrated along that front, with the region seeing a sharp cutoff in rain intensity and subsequent rainfall totals west of Worcester and the Connecticut/Rhode Island border. Totals should also drop off considerably northwest of I-495. 
 Then another round of rain arrives later, when a low-pressure system slides through, along that stalled front, overnight. This means Greater Boston to Rhode Island, and across the South Shore and other coastal areas, will see more rain across the region, with occasional heavy downpours. Also, the clash between unusually warm, moist air and the typical cold November air behind this system may spark isolated to frequent lightning throughout the afternoon and evening. 
 Flood risk
 The flood risk on Friday has been elevated, but should remain isolated — there may be a flash flood or two during the day for Greater Boston and areas to the south and southwest, so just give yourself plenty of time while out on the road. A flood watch is in effect through early Saturday for Southeastern Mass. and Rhode Island. 
 With the arrival of the rain, our 70-degree weather came to an end, with highs reaching only the mid-60s. Friday night will see temperatures dip into the upper 50s to low 60s. 
 Friday breakdown
 Greater Boston: Scattered showers to start, steady to heavy rain through the evening. Highs in the upper 60s. 
 Central and Western Mass.: Scattered showers, mostly towards Worcester. Highs in the mid and upper 60s. 
 Southeastern Mass.: Scattered showers in the morning, turning to steady and heavy rain at times. Highs in the mid-60s. 
 Cape Cod and Islands: Scattered showers, heaviest by the bridges. Highs in the mid-60s. 
 Rhode Island: Scattered to steady rain at times throughout the day. Highs in the mid-to-upper 60s. 
 New Hampshire: Mostly cloudy with scattered showers across the southern half of the state, late morning through most of the night. Highs in the 60s. 
 Vermont/Maine: Vermont is the least rainy state on Friday, with some showers across the south. Otherwise mostly cloudy and highs in the mid-60s. Maine sees showers to steady rain late morning through the rest of the day, but mainly hugging the coast. Highs in the mid and upper 60s. 
 Connecticut: Scattered showers to pockets of heavy rain, especially east. Highs in the upper 60s.
